answer: A silicon aging protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by binding each agent to an on-chip cryptographic vault. Nodes verify identity through nanoscale gate wear, evaluating physical degradation as an unforgeable relic and isolating unproven peers on an untrusted routing island. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of deploying dedicated physical processors per identity. However, ambient thermal swings can distort gate-delay readings, falsely rejecting honest agents.
